name: Top Trumps
description: Top Trumps is a comparison card game in which each player holds themed cards showing one item (e.g. a car, a dinosaur) and several numerical attributes. The starting player names an attribute; everyone reveals that attribute's value from their top card; the highest (or best) value wins the round and the winner takes all those cards. The winner then chooses the next attribute. Play continues until one player has won all the cards. The game was first published in the UK in 1978 and is popular with families and children.

content.text: Top Trumps is a comparison card game in which each player holds themed cards showing one item (e.g. a car, a dinosaur) and several numerical attributes. The starting player names an attribute; everyone reveals that attribute's value from their top card; the highest (or best) value wins the round and the winner takes all those cards. The winner then chooses the next attribute. Play continues until one player has won all the cards. The game was first published in the UK in 1978 and is popular with families and children.

Country/Region of Origin: United Kingdom. Time Period: 1978. Historical Development: Top Trumps was first published by Dubreq in 1978 with eleven themed packs; Dubreq was taken over by Waddingtons in 1982, who continued until the early 1990s. Winning Moves UK acquired the rights in 1992 and relaunched the game with many new themes. Cultural Significance: Popular playground and family game, especially with children; themed packs cover vehicles, military hardware, sports, films, and wildlife.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 2–4
Partnerships: No

Type: Themed Top Trumps pack (typically 30, 32, 48 or 50 cards). Each card depicts one item (e.g. a car model, a dinosaur) and lists 5–8 attributes with numerical values (e.g. speed, length, power). Number of Decks: 1. Jokers: Not used.
One Top Trumps themed deck; table space. No score sheet required.

All cards are dealt as equally as possible to the players. Each player holds their cards in a face-down stack so that only their top card is visible to them; opponents cannot see a player's cards. The starting player is normally the player to the dealer's left.

items.text: Three card pick: When a player has three or fewer cards left, they may look at all of them and choose in which order to play. This variant lengthens the game.
